Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955).)[(2) It extends to the
whole of Pakistan] ; (The word "and" and sub‑section

Definition

THE LIVE﷓STOCK IMPORTATION ACT, 1898
THE LIVE‑STOCK IMPORTATION ACT, 1898
(For Statement of Objects and Reasons, see
Gazette of India, 1898, Pt. V, p. 282; and for Proceedings in Council, see
ibid., Pt. VI, pp. 362 and 364.)
ACT No. IX OF 1898
[12th
August, 1898]
An Act to make better provision for the regulation of the importation
of live‑stock.
2. Definition----In this Act, unless there is anything repugnant in
the subject or context,‑
(a) the expression
"infectious or contagious disorders" includes tick‑pest,
anthrax, glanders, farcy, scabies and any other disease or disorder which may
be specified by the (Subs. by A. O., 1937, for "G.
G. in C.".)[Central Government] by notifica tion in the (Subs. ibid., for "Gazette of India".)[official
Gazette]; and
(b) "live‑stock"
includes horses, kine, camels, sheep and any other animal which may be
specified by the (Subs. by A. O., 1937, for "G. G.
in C.".)[Central Government] by notification (For Notifn. specifying mules, asses, bullocks, buffaloes,
goats and swine as live‑stock, see Gaz. of India. 1944, Pt. I, p. 1101.)
in the (Subs. ibid., for "Gazette of India".)
[official Gazette].

Power to regulate importation of live-stock

THE LIVE﷓STOCK IMPORTATION ACT, 1898
THE LIVE‑STOCK IMPORTATION ACT, 1898
(For Statement of Objects and Reasons, see
Gazette of India, 1898, Pt. V, p. 282; and for Proceedings in Council, see
ibid., Pt. VI, pp. 362 and 364.)
ACT No. IX OF 1898
[12th
August, 1898]
An Act to make better provision for the regulation of the importation
of live‑stock.
3. Power to regulate importation of live-stock---‑(1) The (Subs. by A. O., 1937, for "G. G. in C.".)[Central
‑Government] may, by notification(For Notifn.
prohibiting import except the Bombay, Calcutta, Karachi and Madras, see Gaz. of
India, 1944, Pt. I, p. 1101.) in the (Subs. by
A. O.,1937, for "Gazette of India".)[official Gazette]
regulate, restrict or prohibit, in such manner and to such extent as (Subs. ibid., for "he".)[it] may think fit,
the bringing or taking, by sea or land, into (Subs. by
the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd
Sch. (with effect from the 10th October, 155), for "the
Provinces and the Capital of the Federation" which had been subs. by A.
O., 1949, Arts. 3(2) and 4, for "British India".)[Pakistan] or
any specified place therein, of any live‑stock which may be liable to be
affected by infectious or contagious disorders, and of any fodder, dung,
stables‑litter, clothing, harness or fittings appertaining to live stock
or that may have been in contact therewith.
(2) A notification under sub‑section
(1) shall operate as if it had been issued under section 19 of the Sea Customs
Act, 1878, and the officers of customs at every port shall have the same powers
in respect of any live‑stock or thing, with regard to the importa tion of
which such a notification has been issued, and the vessel containing the same,
as they have for the time being in respect of any article the importation of
which is regulated, restricted or prohibited by the law relating to sea customs
and the vessel con taining the same; and the enactments for the time being in
force relating to sea customs or any such article or vessel shall apply
accordingly. VIII of 1878.

Power for Provincial Government to make rules

THE LIVE﷓STOCK IMPORTATION ACT, 1898
THE LIVE‑STOCK IMPORTATION ACT, 1898
(For Statement of Objects and Reasons, see
Gazette of India, 1898, Pt. V, p. 282; and for Proceedings in Council, see
ibid., Pt. VI, pp. 362 and 364.)
ACT No. IX OF 1898
[12th
August, 1898]
An Act to make better provision for the regulation of the importation
of live‑stock.
4. Power for Provincial Government to make rules-----‑(1) The
(Subs. by A. O., 1937, for "L. G.".)[Provincial
Government] may (The words "subject to the control
of the G. G. in C." rep., ibid.)* * * make rules(For rules in respect of East Bengal, see Dacca Gazette, 1950,
Pt. I, pp. 362‑363.) for the detention, inspection, disinfection
or destruction of imported live‑stock, and of fodder, dung, stable‑litter,
clothing, harness or fittings appertaining to imported live‑stock or that
may have been in contact therewith, and for regulating the powers and duties of
the officers whom it may appoint in this behalf.
(2) In making any rule under this
section the (Subs. by A. O., 1949, Arts. 3(2) and 4,
for "British India".)[Pro vincial Government] may direct that
a breach thereof shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one thousand
rupees.
sections.punishment:
punishable with fine which may extend to one thousand
rupees.

5. Protection to persons acting under Act. No suit, prosecution or other legal
proceeding still lie against any person for anything in good faith done or
intended to be done under this Act.
